assigned.title: Playback-session candidate wire bounds match StreamCandidate bounds
assigned.acceptance: playbackSessionCandidateSchema uses THE SAME AUTHORITATIVE id and providerId limits as the StreamCandidate contract -- the exported MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_ID_CHARS and MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_PROVIDER_ID_CHARS -- and NOT copied numeric literals. PL-0708 exported those constants for exactly this reason; a copied literal would recreate the defect one layer out, which is the defect this task exists to close. Required: an oversized resolved candidate CANNOT RE-EXPAND ON THE SESSION WIRE after passing through another producer seam, which is the actual risk -- the contract bound governs what a provider may produce, and a second unbounded restatement downstream means the bound stops at the seam; fixture and Wikidata legitimate identifiers remain accepted, because a bound that rejects a real upstream id is an outage rather than a fix; tests cover the EXACT MAXIMUM, MAXIMUM PLUS ONE, and the serialized response, since a bound tested only from above does not prove the boundary is where it is claimed to be; reason and error output does not echo the oversized value; and NO SECOND INDEPENDENT BOUND VOCABULARY IS INTRODUCED. Note while working: playbackSessionCandidateSchema also carries unbounded uri and mimeType. They are not named in the reviewer's acceptance and are not in scope by default -- if they warrant bounds, say so and let the reviewer rule rather than adding them quietly.

review.title: Catalog ingestion is scheduled and stored, not re-run per query
review.acceptance: Catalog answers are served from stored ingested state refreshed on a schedule, rather than by running a full ingestion pass per query. TODAY THE ADAPTER RUNS ONE FULL runIngestionPass PER QUERY, which is correct for a seam and wrong for a deployment: it makes every page view an outbound crawl, ties response time to an upstream service, and scales the load on that service with this product's traffic. Required: the freshness and next-pass planning PL-0305 already built is what DRIVES the schedule rather than being recomputed alongside it; an answer still carries its age and stated staleness policy, so nothing becomes fresher by being cached; tombstones survive a refresh, because a work withdrawn upstream must not reappear from stored state; a refresh that fails leaves the previous state served AND SAYS SO, rather than emptying the catalog or silently serving stale data as current; and rights and availability are re-evaluated against stored records rather than trusted from the pass that stored them, since a rights basis can lapse. The reviewer noted that PL-0305 is NOT to be described as having delivered a deployed ingestion worker; this task is where that claim would become true.

typecheck.evidence: npx turbo run typecheck lint build --force, exit 0, 33 of 33 tasks (11 typecheck, 11 lint, 11 build), 0 cached. Re-run by the lead independently of the implementer, not carried from its report. NEW MODULES: packages/catalog-ingestion/src/store.ts (the CatalogStore port, createInMemoryCatalogStore, and applyPassToSnapshot -- a PURE function holding the whole rule for what a pass does to stored state, so the in-memory store is a closure around it and a durable store would be a transaction around it) and packages/catalog-ingestion/src/schedule.ts (validateCatalogRefreshSchedule, catalogRefreshCadence, assessStoredFreshness, planCatalogRefresh, refreshCatalogIfDue). NO TIMER EXISTS IN THE PACKAGE: no setInterval, no setTimeout, no clock read; time is a parameter throughout, as freshness.ts requires. THE TYPE SYSTEM CARRIES ONE DELIBERATE COMPROMISE AND IT IS NAMED: CatalogIngestionRuntime.schedule is OPTIONAL rather than required, because apps/web/src/lib/server-bootstrap.ts line 390 returns the runtime as an object literal and is OFF THIS TASK'S SURFACE -- a required field would stop that file compiling and a deployment would then have no catalog at all. Verified at the line rather than assumed. An absent schedule is the package's named policy_not_stated, which refreshes on every read and publishes NO freshness verdict, rather than a defaulted policy: without an operator statement nothing may be described as fresh.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 20 of 20 tasks, 0 cached, 2712 passed 1 skipped against a 2667/1 baseline: +45, and the arithmetic was recomputed by the lead from the per-package figures rather than taken from the implementer's table (100+67+68+47+208+252+373+260+288+148+901 = 2712). catalog-ingestion 117 to 148 (+31: store.test.ts 14, schedule.test.ts 17), web 887 to 901 (+14: the adapter suite 14 to 28). test:scripts 0, repo:validate 0, ai:validate 0. THE MUTATION EVIDENCE WAS RE-RUN BY THE LEAD, not accepted on report. Three mutants planted and observed independently. M1, delete the read-time checkRightsBasis block from the adapter: 2 adapter tests fail, 26 pass -- 'withholds a stored work whose rights basis is not established' and 'withholds a stored work whose rights reference is not an opaque identifier'. M2, release a tombstone on ANY pass by dropping result.complete from the guard at store.ts:355: 1 store test fails ('does not let a partial pass release a tombstone, even when it returns the work') AND 1 adapter test fails ('keeps a work a complete pass proved gone out of a later partial pass's answer'), which is the cross-layer half. M3 and the remaining mutants in the implementer's table were reported and are recorded here as REPORTED RATHER THAN RE-VERIFIED BY THE LEAD: wholesale tombstone replacement, failed pass emptying works, atMs taken from observedAt, and a fresh store per createCatalogIngestionSource call. THE RED-TO-GREEN FOR CLAUSE 6 IS AGAINST A MUTATION OF THE NEW CODE AND NOT AGAINST THE OLD ADAPTER, and that is stated rather than smoothed over: the old adapter ran a pass per query and held no stored state, so a lapsed rights basis was unreachable there. The rights_basis_not_declared case needs a SEEDED snapshot, because no pass would ever accept a null-basis work -- justified as the state a durable store genuinely produces (written by an older build, another process, or an operator) and the reason createInMemoryCatalogStore takes an initial snapshot. The availability-window case needs no seeding and exercises the same clause end to end. EVERY pass result in the package tests is a real runIngestionPass result against a scripted provider rather than a hand-built object, so no test can assert a complete/tombstonesWithheld combination the pass cannot produce. WHAT THE TESTS DO NOT PROVE, in the implementer's own words and kept: that anything is durable (it is not); that a hosted deployment now avoids a pass per read (it does not, until server-bootstrap.ts states a policy -- see the architecture-review request); that a background worker exists (it does not); and that LIBERTY_CATALOG_MAX_PAGES no longer bounds the visible catalog (it still does, since no pass resumes).

recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

recommended.title: Profile model
recommended.acceptance: Profiles are modelled above authentication rather than inside the auth library, with the active profile carried alongside the session rather than inside the identity record; profile scoping is present in the first migration rather than retrofitted, because that is the part that is expensive to reverse; profiles can be created and selected with authorization tests

recommended.title: GitHub bridge for cross-agent review
recommended.acceptance: GitHub becomes the shared state bridge for Claude Desktop and OpenAI review without manual file copying. SCOPE ADDITION 2026-09-21, on gpt-architect's ARCHITECTURE / CI FINDING at f6dba611346ac53d72901f661a2b21cc12e80eac, which ruled the check belongs here rather than in a competing task: CI mechanically detects an UNDECLARED WORKSPACE IMPORT -- a source file in one workspace importing a local @liberty package that its own package.json does not declare in dependencies. THE EXACT DEFECT THIS MUST CATCH, preserved as the regression case: apps/web/src/lib/server-bootstrap.ts imported @liberty/media-inspection/node/pinned-fetch while apps/web/package.json declared seven @liberty packages and not that one. It reached a reviewer because NO EXISTING GATE CAN SEE IT: the import resolves through the root workspace symlink, so typecheck, lint, build and the unit suites were green, and even npm ci --dry-run returned 0 because npm tolerates a link node that already exists. It was found by a human reader, which is not a detection mechanism. Required of the check: it reads each workspace's own manifest rather than the root's; it resolves subpath imports (@liberty/x/node/y declares @liberty/x); it covers test files as well as source, since server-bootstrap.test.ts carried the same undeclared import; and it fails the build rather than warning, because a warning in a green pipeline is how this one survived. A dry-run install against a populated node_modules does NOT satisfy this and must not be offered as the implementation. NOT IN SCOPE: the reverse direction (a declared dependency nothing imports) is a different and much weaker signal, and adding it would make the check noisy enough to be turned off.
recommended.notes: CI finding folded in 2026-09-21 from the PL-0311 round rather than filed as its own task, on the reviewer's explicit instruction not to open a competing task.
